subject: Post-call: PayGrid model fit evals & next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: PayGrid model fit evals & next steps

Hi Emma — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment:

Recap:
- Primary goal: improve PayGrid's payment-experience assistant accuracy for edge-case reconciliation prompts while keeping latency under 250ms P95 and cost within your current budget envelope.
- Existing baseline: in-house proprietary model (PayGrid-K) used for reconciliation triage.
- Data constraints: no PCI data in evaluation sets; synthetic/obfuscated samples OK.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share the evaluation prompt set and initial benchmark run we did against a few open models plus Redwood-verified variants. See attached CSV + prompt set.
2) Technical deep-dive with Marissa & Dylan next week to go over parity thresholds and failure modes.
3) If an open model meets your acceptance thresholds, we’ll scope a pilot for 2k daily queries and a success metric for precision@top1 and regression delta vs PayGrid-K.

Attachments: paygrid-benchmark-results.csv, prompt-set-v1.json

Let me know which time slots work for you next week for the deep-dive — I proposed Tue/Wed 10–12 PT in the calendar invite.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Hi Aditya — thanks for the recap and attachments. Quick notes: we can use the obfuscated reconciliation logs for the evals; Alex will own the data handoff.

A couple of questions after a quick skim of the CSV:
- Which specific open models did you run? I see model IDs but not clear mapping to quantization/variants.
- What acceptance thresholds are you proposing for parity vs our PayGrid-K baseline? We’re typically conservative on precision for fraud/finance flows.

Tue 10:30 PT works for us for the technical deep-dive — adding Alex and I to the invite.

Best,
Emma

emma.chan@paygrid.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Alex Rivers <alex.rivers@paygrid.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: PayGrid model fit evals & next steps

Emma — thanks, great. To answer your questions in short: we ran three open models (Llama-3-13B-v2, Pythia-12B-qlora, Mistral-7B-Instruct) and two Redwood-verified variants (Llama-3-13B-v2-8bit and Mistral-7B-q8). The CSV includes per-prompt precision/recall/latency columns and the model_id mapping is in the first sheet.

Proposed acceptance thresholds (initial, subject to technical review):
- Precision@top1: within 2% absolute of PayGrid-K on the reconciliation prompt set
- Latency: P95 <= 250ms in your target region (us-west) with batched traffic profile
- Regression safety: no more than 1.5% absolute drop on high-risk prompt subset (fraud/financial corrections)

If an open model meets those thresholds we can scope the pilot. If none meet parity, we’ll propose an approach: either fine-tune a top open candidate (few-shot + LoRA) or use Redwood routing to keep PayGrid-K for high-risk prompts while serving open models for the rest to reduce costs.

Attached also: redwood-model-recommendations.pdf with short notes on tradeoffs (quality vs cost). We’ll walk through this in the deep-dive.

See you Tue 10:30 PT.

— Aditya

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Chan <emma.chan@paygrid.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Alex Rivers <alex.rivers@paygrid.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: PayGrid model fit evals & next steps

Hi all — quick technical note ahead of the deep-dive. I ran a focused slice of the prompt set overnight and flagged the following observations:

1) Model-level summary (rough):
- Mistral-7B-Instruct: best latency (P95 ~120ms) but shows consistent undergeneration on multi-step reconciliation prompts, precision delta ~4% vs PayGrid-K.
- Llama-3-13B-v2-8bit: closest to parity on precision (delta ~1.1%) but P95 is around 320ms on our default serving config; with quantization tweaks and batching it can drop toward 240–260ms.
- Pythia-12B-qlora: mixed quality; very cost-effective but higher variance on corner cases.

2) Acceptance guidance: if your risk tolerance requires <=2% precision delta across the entire eval set AND hard P95 <=250ms, Llama-3-13B-v2-8bit looks like the best candidate for a pilot with minor infra tuning. If PayGrid requires absolute parity on the high-risk subset, plan for a small LoRA fine-tune or keep PayGrid-K gated for those prompts.

3) Next steps for the pilot scope:
- Infra: we’ll provision a dedicated instance group for the L3-13B-8bit pilot to hit P95 targets.
- Eval: we suggest a shadow pass for 3 days to measure real traffic distribution before routing live.
- Success metrics: precision@top1 within 2% absolute and a regression delta on high-risk subset <=1.5%.

I’ll put technical notes and a short runbook in the Drive folder (link in the related_links). Happy to dig into any of the examples in the prompt set during the call.

— Marissa
